title: Sec jotter — sprint mind-dump (Siena)
content:
Quick brain dump for the sprint — making little progress unless I force structure. Mostly thinking aloud: what we actually need to show an auditor vs what infra needs to harden.

Goal: assemble minimal traceable evidence sets for Access, Change Mgmt, Logging, KMS, and Deployment Isolation. Short-term deliverable: 1 control narrative + 3 pieces of evidence per control by end of March.

High-level notes / open questions:
- Evidence bucket naming: do we centralize under /evidence/soc2/2026/<team>/ or keep team-owned folders? Pros/cons: centralized easier for audit, team-owned better for daily ops. Need consistency for automated snapshot script. TODO: propose naming in SEC-4123.
- Who is owner for Dedicated capacity audit evidence? Likely infra-owner + account exec to sign on contract docs. Omar?
- KMS/HSM: Private customers can bring keys (BYOK) + we have platform KMS integration. Need plain doc that maps: how keys are used, where key material never persists, and who has access (nobody). Also: show API calls that rotate keys (example curl + log lines). Do we have a rotation job? If not, schedule a runbook.

Control mapping rough stubs (ideas to shape into narratives):
1) Access Control (logical) — CC6-ish
  - Narrative: RBAC enforced at Console + API token scopes; SSO + SCIM provisioning for enterprise; service accounts limited by least privilege.
  - Evidence candidates: sample SCIM user creation event (Confluence link + auth logs), IAM role bindings snapshot (exported JSON), an example token with restricted scope and associated audit log showing usage.
  - Gaps: need one documented user deprovisioning flow tied to HR offboarding (link to HR playbook missing). Task: capture a deprovision run from last quarter (ask SRE).

2) Change Management (deploys, code review)
  - Narrative: PR-based flow, CI gating, canary rollouts via console. All config changes recorded in Git with PR descriptions and approvals.
  - Evidence: Git history snippet for a config change, CI/CD run with approval logs, rollout event in Console (timestamped).
  - Gaps: need a signed change policy doc (draft in Confluence). Also need sample emergency change postmortem.

3) Logging & Monitoring
  - Narrative: System and application logs forwarded to central observability (ELK/Datadog). Alerts create JIRA tasks; retention policy set to 1 year for security logs.
  - Evidence: example alert -> JIRA issue ID, export of retention policy screen, sample log lines demonstrating auth failure -> block.
  - Gaps: confirm retention enforcement for Dedicated customer instances (is it same retention? check infra config INF-4321).

4) Key Management
  - Narrative: Keys never exported in plaintext; platform integrates with customer KMS for Private deployments; rotation policy documented.
  - Evidence: architecture diagram (Confluence), KMS audit event sample showing encryption/decryption calls, DB table showing crypto metadata (no keys).
  - Gaps: missing automated rotation job evidence. If rotation is manual we need the runbook + log of executed rotation.

5) Isolation / Private deploys / Dedicated
  - Narrative: Private Control Plane vs customer-managed dataplane, network ACLs, VPC peering, encryption in transit. Dedicated capacity has reserved pools and capacity SLOs.
  - Evidence: network ACL snapshots, VPN/peering config, customer contract snippet for Dedicated, infra topology export.
  - Gaps: need a short note describing fallback behavior (how we degrade to hosted variants) — auditors ask about cross-tenant fallbacks.

Practical to-dos (short):
- [ ] Draft short control narratives (one paragraph each) and drop in Confluence (assign to me by 3/10) — linked to SEC-4123.
- [ ] Export example logs for Access & KMS (ask Logan for help) — target 3/9.
- [ ] Verify Git history examples — collect PRs for last 90 days with approvals.
- [ ] Find one emergency change postmortem & redact (ask release-eng).
- [ ] Create evidence bucket and put README.md describing each file (format, who can touch).

Evidence format proposal (for later automation):
- filename convention: <control>-<artifact-type>-<yyyy-mm-dd>-<owner> (e.g., access-log-2026-03-01-logstash-siena.json)
- metadata header for each artifact: {control, artifact_type, timestamp, source, verified_by} (we can store as small JSON companion file).

Notes to self / friction points:
- Auditors like a narrative + pointer to raw artifacts. Need to avoid giving them a huge heap of stuff with no explanation. Keep evidence lightweight and curated.
- We need buy-in from teams — makes sense to build a tiny checklist template team can fill. Maybe make a small Google Form to collect ownership & artifact pointers.
- Risk question: If a Dedicated customer requests FIPS/HSM certs, what's the minimum proof we can present? (Do we have HSM-attested logs?).

Random scratch thoughts:
- Could script a snapshotter that pulls 1 sample per control each week and puts it in the evidence bucket with a checksum + provenance metadata. Automate retention tagging.
- For KMS events, capture both request and response audit event IDs (so we show that keys are used but not exposed).

Slack reminders/links:
- ping @marta for the log export (told her in #sec-redwood Wednesday)
- drop a note in #platform-ops about Dedicated retention (tag Omar)

Immediate next steps (today):
- write the 1-paragraph narratives and paste into Confluence (15–30 mins)
- create the evidence bucket skeleton (mkdir + README)

Open questions for the next sync with Omar/Marta:
- Who signs off as evidence owner? (per-control vs per-team?)
- Are manual rotation events acceptable if documented and periodic? (we need criteria)
- How to handle customer-provided KMS keys in evidence without exposing customer material? (redaction strategy)

Last note: keep this doc as a working scratchpad. I will prune and publish a cleaner "SOC2 evidence index" when we have 3 controls fully curated.

-----
Personal TODO: 1) stop dithering and file the Confluence page; 2) schedule a 30m sync with Omar next Tue; 3) ask release-eng for one emergency change doc to redact.

Siena
